![badgeEs](https://img.shields.io/badge/leaflet-f1e05a?style=for-the-badge&logo=leaflet)
![badgeEs](https://img.shields.io/badge/d3-f1e05a?style=for-the-badge&logo=d3)
![badgeEs](https://img.shields.io/badge/javascript-darkgreen?style=for-the-badge&logo=javascript)
![badgeEs](https://img.shields.io/badge/html-red?style=for-the-badge&logo=HTML)

## Description

The objective of this project is to offer simple to use code for building webpages to explore multi-dimensional data stored in an Elasticsearch index. Sounds complicated, but isn't: Elasticsearch is just another service to store data (similar to a database but with a focus on search and aggregation), and multidimensional means that each row of data contains many columns,

 The code works out of the box with any Elasticsearch index, customization is possible and sometimes needed to enhance the user experience. The goal is to investigate data integrity and find correlations between fields in your data sets. As a side effect you will get the possibility to automatically create regular aggregations of your datasets (like e.g. monthly statistical data about inhabitant counts in suburbs).

Features:
- Data driven (the default configuration works for every index)
- Vanilla Javascript and few libraries like Leaflet.js and D3.js, no frameworks like react, vue.js or angular
- Simple approaches: just HTML, CSS and Javascript
- Code is organized object oriented
- Customizable for special cases
- Code is representing a library, not a framework
- Code (including all used libraries) is Open Source under MIT license

#### Motivation

So why should you use it, when many office suites offer the possibility to visualize CSV data? The main advantage when using the data explorer is, that you can simply create the dataset of choice at runtime. So you don't have to extract part of the data (like for registration data e.g.: only data of suburbs XXX and YYY or only data of June 2019 or only people from South America) before you start. Instead you filter the data from **one** dataset during the exploration process.

Apart from that maybe you have very sensitive data that should never leave your company or be stored or installed in a cloud. This project can be run on a simple laptop or desktop computer of your choice, preferably but not limited to a linux (or any other unix) operating system. It should also be runnable natively on MacOS or a modern Windows, additionally we already ran it in a docker container. The system is runnable on a standard computer without any internet connection. The software is open source and has no further dependencies, all needed libraries are (open source and) part of the code.

The needed backend for the data, Elasticsearch, is freely available. While switching temporarily to license "Elastic License v2" due to differences with major cloud providers, they added _AGPLv3_ in 2024, which is recognized by the Open Source Initiative (OSI) as an open source license. The differences lead to a fork of Elasticsearch version 7.10.2 named "OpenSearch" in 2021, which is declared to be compatible with Elasticsearch version 7 as well as 8. So _ElasticsearchDataExplorer_ should also be compatible with _OpenSearch_, but we never tested it explicitly.

## Detailed Information

For more information (especially in German for public authorities) please visit the gitlab [wiki page of this project](https://git.opendfki.de/kirchman/esdataexplorer/-/wikis/home). Here you will find details about installation, development or how to simply use the resulting web site. The code is offered for free under the terms of the MIT-License, Owner/Organization: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI GmbH), 2024. The development was supported by the MPSC project (Modellprojekte Smart Cities) funded by the German government. See [https://www.smart-city-dialog.de/programme-und-projekte/modellprojekte-smart-cities](https://www.smart-city-dialog.de/programme-und-projekte/modellprojekte-smart-cities) for more details.

## Installation

#### Basic idea

The _Index Data Explorer_ is a web application, written in HTML and Javascript. So everything you need on the endusers computer is a modern web browser (like e.g. Firefox or Chromium)

##### Prerequisites:
 - WebServer (linke e.g. Apache or Nginx)
 - Elasticsearch Service
 
##### Steps:
 - Add the following folders from toplevel of the project to the document root folder of the webserver or a subdirectory of your choice:
   + config
   + externalPackages
   + i18n
   + src
   + php (* only needed, if the computer running the browser has no acccess to the used Elasticsearch service *)
   + Additionally you need a folder _data_ on toplevel for specific instances, e.g. for some pages in _examples/kosis_
 - copy the HTML pages you want to offer in _your_ Explorer instance to the same folder of the webserver
 - Note: all the HTML pages on toplevel or in one of the folders in subfolder _examples_ can be copied to the document root folder and are functional there (that is: will find their used/imported files like CSS or images or configuration files)
 - Note: check the _examples_ directory to see some proper use cases
 - Adjust the values in the config files used by your HTML pages to the correct index name(s) and base URL. Additionally you can overwrite the default configurations of most javascript modules found in subfolder _src_ in the config files.

For more detailed information refer to the wiki page mentioned above.
